items.title: We’re onto you, Musk
items.author: Jaiden Gales
items.excerpt: The rocketmen gaze starward with no regard for the fragility of Earth The space race is the crowning jewel of capitalism’s flawed obsession with growth. Graphic Harrison Campbell This article originally appeared in The Link Volume 47, Issue 6, published November 24, 2026.
items.leadExcerpt: The original space race was a Cold War competition between the United States and the Soviet Union from the mid-1950s to the mid-1970s to achieve superior space exploration. Now we’re seeing a modern version of this race, driven by billionaires rushing to profit off the great unknown.

items.title: Quebec’s video game industry wants to reclaim its space in cultural circles
items.author: Aïda M. Lopes
items.excerpt: With international recognition secured, the industry is now looking to achieve it at home Pierre-Olivier Leblanc plays a game during the free local gaming hub at Ausgang Plaza on Nov. 14 during the Festival Gros Joueurs. The daylong event showcases video games made in Québec and
items.leadExcerpt: Quebec’s video game industry generates $1.4 billion in annual revenues, according to La Guilde du jeu vidéo du Québec. Yet local talent feels left out of cultural conversations. To bring more attention to locally developed games, industry members gathered at Ausgang Plaza on St-Hubert St. on Nov. 14 for the inaugural Buy a Quebec Video Game Day, held as part of Festival Gros Joueurs. Gamers in the city have likely already bought local games, but they might not know it. Making sure they have that knowledge is the mission of gamesfromquebec.com, a website showcasing local expertise launched by La Guilde.

items.title: The age of rave

items.excerpt: A look into Montreal’s rave culture over 30 years From warehouses to nightclubs, here is how Montreal’s DIY rave scene evolved from the 1990s to today. Graphic Anika Yvette This article originally appeared in The Link Volume 47, Issue 6, published November 24, 2026.
items.leadExcerpt: “I was already kind of used to nightclubs and that kind of environment, but this was very new, like a warehouse, and everything was larger than life. Everything felt so free and different and risky,” Ste-Marie said.

items.leadExcerpt: At around 5 p.m. on Tuesday, Nov. 10, an anonymous group of 50 or so masked and hooded individuals barricaded themselves into a corner of the Henry F. Hall Building mezzanine. They used tables, chairs, couches, newsstands and other university furniture to sequester themselves into an imposing, chaotic bunker. Four hours later, over two dozen heavily armed Service de police de la Ville de Montréal (SPVM) officers entered the university, pepper spray and tear gas in hand, causing all but one of the protesters to flee the building.

items.title: Concordia launches new Sustainability Action Plan, outlining green goals for the next four years
items.author: Eric Klempan
items.excerpt: This semester, Concordia University launched its 2026-30 Sustainability Action Plan (SAP). The strategy outlines sustainability goals to be achieved over the next four years, focusing on five operational streams: climate, biodiversity, procurement, food and waste. The plan also
items.leadExcerpt: This semester, Concordia University launched its 2026-30 Sustainability Action Plan (SAP). The strategy outlines sustainability goals to be achieved over the next four years, focusing on five operational streams: climate, biodiversity, procurement, food and waste. The plan also includes the engagement streams of curriculum and research. Overall, the new goals follow those of the 2020-25 strategy, with the biggest additions being the procurement and biodiversity streams. According to the final progress report of the last SAP, only 72 per cent of targets and 62 per cent of strategies were completed, leaving many initiatives to be completed in the current plan.

items.title: CRUES adopts strike motion for winter 2027, granted it meets threshold support
items.author: Léo Vallet David
items.excerpt: The Coalition de résistance pour l’unité étudiante syndicale has adopted a motion to strike following Feb. 15, 2027, given “20,000 students on three different campuses obtain a General Unlimited Strike mandate” aligned with its campaign.
items.leadExcerpt: This strike would begin following Feb. 15, 2027. This is only a mandate, and not an official call to strike. For this strike to happen, “20,000 students on three different campuses obtain a General Unlimited Strike mandate in the context of the CRUES campaign.” The “militant student union” represents a total of 30,000 members — including Concordia’s Sociology & Anthropology Student Union (SASU), Geography Undergraduate Student Society (GUSS), School of Community and Public Affairs Student Association (SCPASA), and Women’s and Sexuality Studies Student Association (WSSSA).

items.title: Where can you actually go to relax between classes?
items.author: Léa Leblond
items.excerpt: As campus departments consolidate into central buildings, Concordia students and faculty are questioning where to find cost-free, low-pressure third spaces to decompress between lectures.
items.leadExcerpt: For one Concordia communication student, that question sparked a new campus initiative. She is currently surveying her peers on what it takes to build better campus “recharge spaces,” a project backed by a $500 mini-grant from the No Experience Necessary Challenge that echoes the Concordia Student Union (CSU)’s plans for a student-run building.

items.title: The 69th Grammy Awards nominations boast inconsistency
items.author: Aidan Flanagan
items.excerpt: Newness is a concept that the Academy often seems to struggle with, especially when considering the nominees in the Best New Artist category.
items.leadExcerpt: While every year’s nominations look different, one constant remains: the results are met with a mixture of praise, criticism and, more often, confusion. Categories like Best New Artist have been met with the latter, while many nominees in the “Big Three” categories have been received largely well. Record of the Year, Album of the Year and Song of the Year, consisted of names that made sense. Olivia Dean, Olivia Rodrigo and the ever-present Taylor Swift have all appeared with their respective chart-topping songs.

items.title: QUICKSPIN: U2 — Carnaval de Luz
items.author: Anna Dunlop
items.excerpt: After 50 years together, U2 released their 16th studio album, Carnaval de Luz, to celebrate their career, regardless of wins or losses.
items.sourceImageCredit: Photo : Carnaval de Luz Album Cover
items.leadExcerpt: While it makes bold attempts that don’t suit the band’s style and leans into desperate alignments with youth, the record unfortunately can’t settle on one coherent style or sound. It keeps shifting its tone and genre, but it still shows self-awareness and genuine admiration for a long career. The album starts off strong, with a high-energy, nostalgic sound in both “Go (Carnaval de Luz)” and “La Reina.” However, it quickly loses its footing over the next five tracks, becoming slightly overproduced as certain hooks lean toward changing-room music.

items.title: QUICKSPIN: Snoh Aalegra — Legendary Love
items.author: Aidan Flanagan
items.excerpt: Snoh Aalegra has been a long-time favourite among modern R&B fans for her ability to blend the genre’s past and future. Her smoky vocals are reminiscent of an old soul and are often paired with more modern instrumentals.
items.leadExcerpt: Snoh Aalegra has been a long-time favourite among modern R&B fans for her ability to blend the genre’s past and future. Her smoky vocals are reminiscent of an old soul and are often paired with more modern instrumentals. Yet on her first full-length release in five years, Aalegra fully leans into the old R&B days in what will likely become a seminal work in her discography. Legendary Love triumphs in exploring heartbreak and hope for what could have been. “Run Free” opens the album like an ‘80s soul track with warm synths and mid-tempo drums. Synths are consistent throughout this record, drawing endless inspiration from ‘80s pop, soul and neo-soul.

items.title: La place des femmes en photojournalisme : qui a la chance de raconter le monde en images?
items.author: Kim Bouchard
items.excerpt: En cette session d’automne qui touche à sa fin, je m’apprête à terminer, dans quelques mois, un programme de deuxième cycle en journalisme visuel à l’Université Concordia. Comme plusieurs personnes étudiantes de mon âge, je me demande où j’aboutirai à la fin de mon parcours
items.leadExcerpt: En cette session d’automne qui touche à sa fin, je m’apprête à terminer, dans quelques mois, un programme de deuxième cycle en journalisme visuel à l’Université Concordia. Comme plusieurs personnes étudiantes de mon âge, je me demande où j’aboutirai à la fin de mon parcours académique. Mais une chose est certaine : ce que je souhaite profondément, c’est devenir photojournaliste. Ce qui me préoccupe toutefois, c’est mon avenir dans cette profession en tant que femme, et en tant que femme issue d’une minorité visible. Quelle sera ma place dans un domaine, encore aujourd’hui, largement dominé par les hommes? Cette inquiétude m’amène à me poser des questions qui dépassent mon propre futur : Qui a accès à la production et à la narration des histoires visuelles dans les médias d’information? Quels points de vue et quelles réalités y sont représentés visuellement?

items.title: SPVM arrests two former Montreal police officers
items.author: Nicolas Tremblay
items.excerpt: The former officers were part of the officers fired from Station 39 earlier this month Montreal police confirmed that two former officers from Station 39 arrested on Nov. 21 were part of the seven officers fired earlier this month. The two officers were arrested for alleged
items.leadExcerpt: Montreal police (SPVM) arrested two former officers on Nov. 21 for alleged discriminatory and racist acts. Both officers were from Station 39 and were part of the seven police officers fired earlier this month, according to the SPVM. Five of the officers were from Station 39, and two were from Station 21, according to SPVM Chief Fady Dagher. They were let go due to allegations of racism, discrimination and misconduct. The two former officers from Station 39 were arrested following a warrant issued by the Director of Criminal and Penal Prosecutions (DPCP) and face charges of assault, criminal harassment and breach of trust, according to Montreal police.

items.excerpt: Deux compétitions sud-américaines ont vu un vainqueur désigné cette fin de semaine. Six fois champions d’Amérique, Boca Juniors a remporté son premier titre international depuis 2008. Au championnat brésilien, le Flamengo a décroché le titre après un match décisif contre le seul
items.sourceImageCredit: Image tirée du compte Instagram de Boca Juniors
items.leadExcerpt: Deux compétitions sud-américaines ont vu un vainqueur désigné cette fin de semaine. Six fois champions d’Amérique, Boca Juniors a remporté son premier titre international depuis 2008. Au championnat brésilien, le Flamengo a décroché le titre après un match décisif contre le seul adversaire qui pouvait encore le dépasser dans le classement. Le club argentin ramène, pour la troisième fois de son histoire, la Copa Sudamericana à Buenos Aires. Depuis la Recopa sud-américaine de 2008, le Boca Juniors n’avait remporté aucun trophée international. La Copa Sudamericana est l’équivalent de la Ligue Europa en Amérique du sud. Le vainqueur obtient également une place en phase de groupe de la Libertadores de l’année suivante.

items.title: Archivistique : Étudier le passé comme carrière d’avenir
items.author: Jeanne Le Goff
items.excerpt: Les étudiant·e·s en archivistique entament leurs études sous le signe de l’incertitude. La multiplication des coupes budgétaires dans les institutions et l’essor du numérique transforment en profondeur leur futur métier, forçant une réinvention de celui-ci. Pour mieux comprendre
items.leadExcerpt: Les étudiant·e·s en archivistique entament leurs études sous le signe de l’incertitude. La multiplication des coupes budgétaires dans les institutions et l’essor du numérique transforment en profondeur leur futur métier, forçant une réinvention de celui-ci. Pour mieux comprendre cette réalité, Quartier Libre est allé à leur rencontre, ainsi qu’à celle de spécialistes du secteur. Bien qu’il soit aujourd’hui en pleine évolution, le métier d’archiviste a longtemps souffert d’une image stéréotypée. « Traditionnellement, les archivistes ont toujours eu l’image vieillotte d’une personne qui est dans le fond de son sous-sol et attend qu’il y ait des visiteurs ou des chercheurs qui viennent consulter ses archives », explique l’experte-conseil en gestion de l’information dans le domaine de l’éducation Florence Rousseau.

items.title: The many controversies of the 2026 WNBA season
items.author: Trent Deschamps-Coinner
items.excerpt: The Golden State Valkyries made history by winning the championship in their second season, but the WNBA’s remarkable year was also marked by controversies over race, gender and politics.
items.leadExcerpt: The 2026 Women’s National Basketball Association (WNBA) season was another reminder that sports and politics are impossible to separate. Fans only enjoyed a couple of months of pure hoops during the 2026 season before the league became a centre of culture-war discussion points and right-wing political grifting. The season took place on the heels of a long negotiation surrounding the collective bargaining agreement between the WNBA Players’ Union and the league. There was a real possibility that the players would have gone on strike, potentially disrupting the season. However, last March, WNBA players unanimously voted to accept a new seven-year collective bargaining agreement, and the WNBA season proceeded as scheduled, tipping off May 8, 2026.

items.leadExcerpt: Les émotions derrière la conquête du trophée Gilles-Courteau sont revenues à la surface au Cinéma Odyssée. Les Saguenéens de Chicoutimi y ont présenté, en avant-première, leur série documentaire La coupe ou rien, une production qui sera diffusée sur Crave dès le 26 novembre. Cette série replonge dans le parcours marquant de l’équipe lors de la dernière saison. Les trois épisodes d’environ 30 minutes ont été projetés consécutivement devant un public invité composé notamment des familles d’accueil, des joueurs de l’édition championne, des membres de la formation actuelle et des représentants des médias. La coupe était également sur place dès 16 h, alors que se déroulait la cérémonie de remise des bagues aux membres de l’équipe.

items.title: Le mont Apica dans la mire de l’éolien régional
items.author: Charline Lachance
items.excerpt: Alors que le Comité Synergie Éolien souhaite faire du Saguenay–Lac-Saint-Jean un pôle de développement éolien, le parc de Saint-Gédéon témoigne de la présence déjà établie de cette énergie dans la région. (Photo : Charline Lachance) Le Comité Synergie Éolien a annoncé deux
items.leadExcerpt: Le Comité Synergie Éolien a annoncé deux projets éoliens majeurs lundi pour le Saguenay–Lac-Saint-Jean. Synergie Éolien, Hydro-Québec et Nergica collaboreront en vue d’une étude pour l’implantation potentielle d’éoliennes sur le mont Apica ainsi qu’un Ceolloque sur les énergies renouvelables au mois de juin. Des mâts de mesure seront installés prochainement sur le mont Apica par Hydro-Québec. L’objectif est d’évaluer si les conditions seraient idéales pour construire un parc éolien.

items.title: What went wrong with the McGill Law controversy
items.author: Eve Learns
items.excerpt: A debate about rehabilitation became a question of journalistic responsibility For many, this is not someone who is deserving of a second chance, especially at such a prestigious institution. Graphic Isobel Budding This article originally appeared in The Link Volume 47, Issue 5,
items.leadExcerpt: He was convicted of second-degree murder and attempted murder for two violent attacks committed in British Columbia in 1984. Eventually, his criminal past became known among the student body, which resulted in some students anonymously reaching out to the CBC. Shortly thereafter, other news outlets began reporting on the story, which further sensationalized an already controversial issue. Over the weekend of Oct. 16 to Oct. 18, CTV, the Montreal Gazette and La Presse all came out with their own article on the “McGill murderer,” further pressuring McGill for a response.

items.leadExcerpt: « Après la disparition du papier, on pourrait bien assister à la disparition d’Internet. » C’est ainsi que Benoît Chartier, vice-président du conseil d’administration de News Media Canada et président du conseil d’administration d’Hebdos Québec, décrit le marché numérique depuis l’arrivée des outils d’intelligence artificielle générative.

items.title: Cinq nouvelles de la semaine
items.author: Samuel Girard
items.excerpt: Voici les nouvelles qui ont marqué l’actualité des derniers jours. Pour consulter les nouvelles de la semaine passée, cliquer ici.
items.leadExcerpt: Un rapport de Statistique Canada révèle que 45 % des femmes ont vécu de la violence conjugale au cours de leur vie, contre 35 % des hommes. Le rapport porte sur trois formes de violences conjugales : les violences sexuelles, physiques et psychologiques. Dans toutes ces catégories, les femmes victimes sont majoritaires, particulièrement dans le cadre de violences sexuelles, où elles sont cinq fois plus nombreuses que les hommes à en être victimes.

items.leadExcerpt: Après 23 parties, le Canadiens présente une fiche de quatorze victoires, cinq défaites et quatre revers en temps supplémentaire. Ce bilan est bon pour le troisième rang de la division Atlantique et le cinquième rang de toute la Ligue nationale de hockey (LNH), malgré plusieurs blessures importantes. Le Canadien doit composer avec plusieurs blessures depuis le début de la campagne. Mike Matheson a manqué quatorze parties, Nick Suzuki, six, tandis que Kaiden Guhle, Chris Kreider et Josh Anderson en ont manqué quatre. Ivan Demidov, quant à lui, n’a disputé que deux matchs cette saison. Zachary Bolduc a également raté la dernière rencontre et on attend encore des nouvelles concernant la durée de son abscence.

À travers un langage chimérique chronically online, une mise en scène surstimulante et des personnages tragi-comiques, l’histoire décortique la solitude humaine et notre besoin d’appartenance à l’ère d’une modernité surconnectée.

items.title: Will Montreal learn from New York about protest and police?
items.author: Nicolas Tremblay
items.excerpt: Montreal Mayor Soraya Martinez Ferrada could take a similar approach to New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani Montreal police first started dispersing the protester crowd at around 3:20 p.m. on René-Lévesque Blvd. during Nov. 13’s protest. Photo Yann Rifflard
items.leadExcerpt: Montreal's police response to the Nov. 13 student protest came under scrutiny at a city council meeting on Nov. 16, where opposition councillors and citizens questioned the use of force against demonstrators. Thousands of protesters took to the streets on Nov. 13 to protest austerity in education. That day, Montreal police officers used tear gas, pepper spray and shields to disperse crowds. In the aftermath, protesters alleged that multiple injuries were caused by Service de police de la Ville de Montréal (SPVM) officers.
